belief: If I don’t speak in tongues, I don’t have the Holy Spirit.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you don’t speak in tongues you don’t have the Holy Spirit, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A church where speaking in tongues was treated as the main proof of being a real believer. Feeling left out or judged when others prayed in tongues and you did not. Pressure to produce an experience you never had. Comparing your quiet faith with other people’s more expressive worship. Christians differ on the place of tongues today, but Scripture is clear on the main question: every believer has the Spirit.
teaches: Every person who belongs to Christ has the Holy Spirit. Believers are sealed with the Spirit when they hear and believe the gospel. Paul asks, “Do all speak in tongues?” and the expected answer is no. The Spirit gives different gifts to different people, as He chooses. The clearest evidence of His presence is not one gift, but His fruit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
self_statements: I must not really be saved.
Something is wrong with me spiritually.
God gave the Spirit to everyone but me.
If I had more faith, I would speak in tongues.
Others are closer to God than I am.
errors: Turning one gift that some receive into a test everyone must pass.
Believing you either have this gift or have no Spirit at all.
Measuring your walk with God by someone else’s experience.
Ignoring the fruit of the Spirit already growing in your life.
Concluding “I feel left out, so God must have left me out.”
questions: What does Romans 8:9 say about everyone who belongs to Christ?
When Paul asks, “Do all speak in tongues?” what answer does he expect?
Who decides which gifts each believer receives?
What fruit of the Spirit can I see growing in my life?
Is this test coming from Scripture or from one group’s experience?
Did I believe in Christ? Then what does Ephesians 1:13 say happened?
Can I respect believers who speak in tongues without doubting my own salvation?
truth: If I belong to Christ, I have the Holy Spirit. I was sealed with the Spirit when I believed the gospel. The Spirit gives different gifts to different people as He chooses, and no single gift is the test of His presence. I can look for His fruit in my life and use the gifts He has given me.
hw_questions: What does Romans 8:9 say about all who belong to Christ?
Does Paul expect all believers to speak in tongues?
Who decides which gifts I receive?
What fruit of the Spirit is growing in me?
Is this test from Scripture or from one group?
What happened when I believed the gospel?
hw_truths: If I belong to Christ, I have the Holy Spirit.
I was sealed with the Spirit when I believed.
The Spirit gives gifts as He chooses.
His fruit in my life shows His presence.
I am not a second-class Christian.
I can honor others’ gifts and trust my own.
log: Each day, write one way I saw love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, or self-control in my life.
name_example: And in Him, having heard and believed the word of truth—the gospel of her salvation—Sarah was sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.

prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You that You live in everyone who belongs to Christ, including me. Help me reject the lie that I do not have You because I lack one gift. Grow Your fruit in my life, show me the gifts You have given me, and help me use them to serve others. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

God’s presence and grace challenge shame and the need to win everyone’s approval.
Christ’s saving work answers condemnation, shame, and fear of separation from God.
